questions.question: What is the main difference between lists and tuples in Python?
options: Lists use square brackets, tuples use parentheses
Lists are mutable (can be changed), tuples are immutable (cannot be changed)
Lists can only store numbers, tuples can store any data type
questions.explanation: The key difference is mutability. Lists can be modified after creation (items can be added, removed, or changed), while tuples cannot be modified once created. This immutability makes tuples useful for storing fixed data that shouldn't change.

questions.question: Which of the following will cause a TypeError?
questions.explanation: Trying to change an element in a tuple using index assignment (my_tuple[0] = 10) will cause a TypeError because tuples are immutable. You can access elements, slice tuples, and reassign the entire variable, but you cannot modify individual elements.

questions.question: When should you use a tuple instead of a list?
options: When you need to add or remove items frequently
When you want to store data that should remain constant, like coordinates or RGB values
When you need to sort the data
When working with large amounts of data only
questions.explanation: Tuples are best for storing fixed data that shouldn't change, such as coordinates (x, y), RGB color values (255, 0, 0), or days of the week. Their immutability provides protection against accidental modification and makes them suitable as dictionary keys.
